deviation: The draft removes Arcadia's right to terminate for convenience entirely (12.1), allowing exit only for uncured material breach or insolvency. This is a loss of a core playbook right and is worse than the fallback (90 days' notice after 12 months), locking Arcadia in and leaving it liable for fees for the full term. Section 12.3 also keeps all accrued/invoiced fees payable and cuts off the Customer's use of the Services on termination.
suggested_text: 12.1 The Customer may terminate this Agreement for convenience at any time by giving 30 days' written notice to the Supplier, without penalty or early termination fee. 12.2 Either Party may terminate this Agreement for cause by written notice if the other Party commits a material breach and fails to remedy it within thirty (30) days after written notice describing the breach, or if the other Party becomes insolvent, makes a general assignment for the benefit of creditors, or becomes subject to bankruptcy or similar proceedings that are not dismissed within a reasonable period. 12.3 Termination or expiry shall not affect accrued rights or liabilities. Upon termination for any reason, the Customer shall pay only Fees properly accrued for Services delivered up to the effective date of termination, and the Supplier shall refund any prepaid Fees for Services not yet provided. Sections 1, 4 (as to accrued amounts), 7, 8, 9.3, 10, 11, 12.3, 13 and 14 shall survive.
